name: Triton Inference Server (observability surface: request-shaped core metrics, LLM metrics only if a backend registers them)
notable_features: Rich, well-documented request-level metrics with type selection via `--metrics-config` (counter, summary or histogram per family since 23.04)

`nv_inference_pending_request_count` is the honest queue-depth metric and the docs go out of their way to define it: requests received by Triton core but not yet started by any model instance, incremented on enqueue and decremented when a backend is about to execute. The docs also list the several places a request can be pending (default scheduler backlog, dynamic batcher queue, sequence batcher queues, rate limiter queues) and the places it will not be (ensemble scheduler, frontends)

Counts distinguish request from inference from execution - `nv_inference_request_success`, `nv_inference_request_failure{reason=REJECTED|CANCELED|BACKEND|OTHER}`, `nv_inference_count` (a batch of n counts as n), `nv_inference_exec_count` (batches) - and the docs walk through worked examples of batch-1+batch-1 giving Request 2 / Inference 2 / Execution 1
OpenTelemetry as an alternative trace backend via `--trace-config mode=opentelemetry --trace-config opentelemetry,url=<endpoint>`, with context propagation supported
hardware_caveats: Triton itself has NO TTFT, TPOT, KV cache usage, preemption or token-throughput metric. `nv_inference_first_response_histogram_ms` measures time to the first RESPONSE, which for a streaming LLM backend is the first chunk delivered, not necessarily the first decoded token, and for a non-streaming backend is essentially the whole request

Everything LLM-specific has to be supplied by the backend through the custom metrics API (TRITONSERVER_MetricFamily*). The metrics doc points at the TensorRT-LLM and vLLM backends for this. If you write your own backend, the core metrics are all you get

The TRT-LLM backend's LLM metrics are a handful of label-switched gauges rather than named metrics: `nv_trt_llm_request_metrics{request_type="waiting|context|scheduled|max|active"}`, `nv_trt_llm_kv_cache_block_metrics{kv_cache_block_type="fraction|tokens_per|used|free|max"}`, `nv_trt_llm_inflight_batcher_metrics{inflight_batcher_specific_metric=...}`, `nv_trt_llm_general_metrics{general_type=...}`, `nv_trt_llm_disaggregated_serving_metrics{disaggregated_serving_type="kv_cache_transfer_ms"|"request_count"}`, `nv_trt_llm_runtime_memory_metrics{memory_type=...}`. Querying these means filtering on the label, not naming the metric
Those TRT-LLM backend metrics need Triton 23.11 or later; before 23.12 the base `nv_inference_*` metrics report 0 for this backend

Triton OTel timestamps come from the system clock while Triton's own trace API uses a steady (monotonic) clock, so a trace captured in one mode cannot be compared numerically against a trace captured in the other
Ensemble failure accounting double-counts and loses the reason: a failing component model reports reason=REJECTED while the ensemble reports reason=OTHER with count=2 for the same failure
best_for: Serving many different model types behind one endpoint where a uniform request-level metric set matters more than LLM-specific insight
Tracing an ensemble or BLS request end to end, since each composing model contributes its own model and compute spans
Choosing your own latency metrics via `--metrics-config` (counters for cheap cumulative tracking, summaries for quantiles, histograms for SLO buckets)
avoid_for: Getting LLM observability from the core server - it will not give you TTFT or KV cache occupancy
Mixing OTel-mode and Triton-mode traces in one time series analysis
notes: Metric names transcribed from docs/user_guide/metrics.md in the main branch. Full core set: counters `nv_inference_count`, `nv_inference_exec_count`, `nv_inference_request_success`, `nv_inference_request_failure`, gauge `nv_inference_pending_request_count`; latency counters `nv_inference_request_duration_us`, `nv_inference_queue_duration_us`, `nv_inference_compute_input_duration_us`, `nv_inference_compute_infer_duration_us`, `nv_inference_compute_output_duration_us`; latency histogram `nv_inference_first_response_histogram_ms`; latency summaries `nv_inference_request_summary_us`, `nv_inference_queue_summary_us`, `nv_inference_compute_input_summary_us`, `nv_inference_compute_infer_summary_us`, `nv_inference_compute_output_summary_us`; GPU `nv_gpu_utilization`, `nv_gpu_power_usage`, `nv_gpu_memory_total_bytes`, `nv_gpu_memory_used_bytes`; CPU `nv_cpu_memory_total_bytes`, `nv_cpu_memory_used_bytes`; pinned memory `nv_pinned_memory_pool_total_bytes`, `nv_pinned_memory_pool_used_bytes`. Granularity is per model (labels model, version), not per request, for most families - an important difference from vLLM/SGLang/TGI, where the histograms are genuinely per-request observations. Trace model: a minimal Triton trace is 3 spans - top level (request received to response sent), model (start, queued, end), compute - with ensembles adding spans per composing model and BLS adding spans for every model in the request. OTel spans carry model_name, model_version, request_id and parent_id as attributes.
